title: Cache and browser storage distinction
learningObjectives: Explain cache and browser storage distinction and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: HTTP caching stores reusable network responses according to cache headers and browser policy. Web Storage and IndexedDB store application data. Cache Storage is a separate API commonly used by service workers to store request/response pairs. These mechanisms have different purposes and lifecycles.
understand.whyItMatters: Confusing caches with application storage can cause stale content or accidental data loss. Cache invalidation, versioning, and privacy must be designed deliberately.
understand.analogy: HTTP cache is a saved copy of a delivery; application storage is a place for the app's own records and preferences.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The example labels distinct storage mechanisms. Their real behaviour is controlled by HTTP headers and browser APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Compare HTTP cache, localStorage, IndexedDB, and Cache Storage. Give one appropriate use and one limitation for each.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
